questions.question: Day 12 Practice (Customer Escalations & Quality (Phase 2)): When talking about booking an auto ride (on weekends), which sentence is grammatically correct for 'My colleague'?

questions.question: Day 12 Vocabulary (Customer Escalations & Quality (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'reach out to'?

options.a: Contact someone for help or information.
options.b: To clean or inspect a physical room thoroughly.
options.c: To perform a daily task hastily without preparation.
options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option A
'reach out to' means: contact someone for help or information. Example: "I will reach out to customer support tomorrow."

questions.question: Day 12 Vocabulary (Customer Escalations & Quality (Phase 2)): What is the exact practical meaning of the phrase 'circle back'?

options.d: To postpone or cancel an activity indefinitely.

questions.explanation:

'circle back' means: return to a topic later for follow-up. Example: "Let us circle back to the timeline discussion."

questions.question:
Day 12 Translation Scenario 1 (Customer Escalations & Quality (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ ఒప్పందంలో కొన్ని మార్పులు చేస్తే బాగుంటుంది."
(Literal attempt: "In agreement some changes if do good.")

options.a: In agreement some changes if do good.
options.b: It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement.
options.c: I am needing to in agreement some changes if do good.
options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option B
Natural Version: "It would be advantageous to incorporate a few revisions into this agreement."

Use executive diplomacy 'It would be advantageous to...'.

questions.question:
Day 12 Translation Scenario 2 (Customer Escalations & Quality (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ముందుగా సమస్య యొక్క మూలకారణాన్ని కనుగొనాలి."
(Literal attempt: "First problem root cause finding wanted.")

options.a: I am needing to first problem root cause finding wanted.
options.b: First problem root cause finding wanted.
options.c: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.d: First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "First and foremost, we must identify the root cause of the issue."

Use 'First and foremost' and 'identify the root cause'.

questions.question:
Day 12 Translation Scenario 3 (Customer Escalations & Quality (Phase 2)):

Telugu: "ఈ టమాటాలు కేజీ ఎంత? కొంచెం తాజావి ఏరి ఇవ్వండి."
(Literal attempt: "These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.")

options.a: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.
options.b: I am needing to these tomatoes kg how much? pick give fresh.
options.c: These tomatoes kg how much? Pick give fresh.
options.d: How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me.

questions.explanation:
Correct: Option D
Natural Version: "How much are these tomatoes per kilo? Please pick out fresh ones for me."

Use 'per kilo' for price and 'pick out' for selection.

questions.question:

options.d: Literal Indian English phrasing without modal polite verbs.

Correct: Option C

Say 'I have a slight headache' instead of literal translations.
